longForm.overview:
🇮🇳 is the emoji of saffron-white-green coded national-identity read — the saffron-and-green banner, the Tiranga coded flex, and the universal 'saffron-white-green pulse' tag for India pride. Where 🇺🇳 reads as neutral-coded diplomacy read and 🏳️‍🌈 reads as rainbow-coded pride read, 🇮🇳 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate saffron-white-green coded identity — a 'saffron-white-green 🇮🇳' heritage check-in or a 'Tiranga pulse 🇮🇳' Team-India reveal. The saffron-and-green banner cue borrows from India's national flag tradition and the modern heritage-coded aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as saffron-white-green coded rather than literal travel-coded flag.

In real-world usage 🇮🇳 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate saffron-white-green energy. A partner sends it on a 'saffron-white-green 🇮🇳' heritage check-in. A friend sends it on a 'Tiranga pulse 🇮🇳' pride reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'saffron-white-green coded 🇮🇳' heritage-month thread. The saffron-and-green banner cue is what makes the emoji feel saffron-white-green coded — it is not just 'flag,' it is 'saffron-white-green coded India-pride moment.'

What separates 🇮🇳 from the rest of the flag family is the saffron-white-green register. The emoji is not saying 'rainbow pride' (🏳️‍🌈), 'black rebellion' (🏴), or 'checkered finish' (🏁). It is saying 'saffron-white-green coded India-coded identity,' which carries a specific national-flag tradition. That is why 🇮🇳 travels especially well on partner heritage check-ins, Team-India reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with saffron-white-green energy.

longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 🇮🇳 in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The saffron-white-green coded banner cue is the wrong tone for any conversation where the moment is somber. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid 🇮🇳 in 'racing' or finish-coded contexts where the saffron-white-green energy feels off. A 'saffron-white-green 🇮🇳' message works for heritage reveal; for finish-coded contexts use 🏁 or a sentence.

Skip 🇮🇳 when you want to communicate a different country. The saffron-white-green coded register is too India-coded for moments that need a literal national flag; use 🇺🇳 or another country flag when the nation needs to land clean.
